steps.title: Tapeology today: the same clean two-page cockpit
steps.narration: This round's work happened behind the scenes — trimming an AI-assistant helper's tool list down to only the pages that still exist — so here is the app looking and working exactly as it did before.
steps.point_out: The navigation bar still shows just two links, Cockpit and Structure, with nothing left over from pages retired earlier.

steps.title: A retired page stays retired
steps.narration: Just to double-check nothing crept back, the old trade-journal address still shows an honest "not found" message instead of any leftover screen.
steps.point_out: Confirms the earlier cleanup is holding steady, not quietly reversed.

expect.text: This page could not be found.

steps.title: Back to the cockpit
steps.narration: Heading back to the home screen, ready to watch a live tape.
steps.point_out: The same simple idle screen, ready for a new watch.

steps.title: Typing a ticker to watch
steps.narration: Typing SIM-BUYER, a built-in scripted simulation, into the ticker field.
steps.point_out: The Watch button, previously dimmed, becomes clickable as soon as a character is typed.

steps.title: Watching a live simulated tape
steps.narration: Clicking Watch starts a live simulated price tape, the same way it always has, and a fresh set of panels appears on screen.
steps.point_out: Six panels appear — Tape State, Quote, Features, Recent Trades, Observations, Event Log — above a live price chart.

steps.title: Live candles keep moving
steps.narration: Switching the chart to 30-second bars shows the tape is genuinely live, not a frozen picture.
steps.point_out: New candlestick bars keep appearing at the right edge of the chart as the simulated tape streams.

expect.text: Logical 30s bars built live from the tape.

steps.title: Stopping cleanly
steps.narration: Clicking Stop ends the watch and returns straight to the plain idle screen.
steps.point_out: No leftover panel or banner appears — just the same clean idle screen as always.

steps.title: Switching to real market data
steps.narration: Switching the data source to Historical, to look at a real recorded trading day instead of a simulation.
steps.point_out: The header switches to the Historical symbol-search layout.

steps.title: Choosing a symbol to replay
steps.narration: Typing AAPL as the symbol to replay.
steps.point_out: The symbol field accepts free-text entry, no dropdown selection required.

steps.title: Choosing a trading day
steps.narration: Typing in a June trading day to replay.
steps.point_out: The date field uses a simple day-month-year format.

steps.title: Jumping straight to the open
steps.narration: One click fills in the market-open replay window.
steps.point_out: The start and end time fields fill in automatically for the 9:30am market open.

steps.title: Watching the real replay
steps.narration: Clicking Watch replays that recorded trading day using real market data.
steps.point_out: The cockpit loads normally with real data, not a "provider unavailable" notice.

steps.title: Real data, clearly labeled
steps.narration: Switching to the 1-hour view shows the same support-and-resistance shading as always, now backed by real data.
steps.point_out: A shaded price band renders on the chart, and the "feed" badge reads "SIP (consolidated)" rather than "Simulated".

steps.title: Exploring the Structure page
steps.narration: The Structure page is the second and last stop in the app, for studying a stock's price levels.
steps.point_out: A simple form is ready for a symbol and an as-of time — no chart or clutter until something is loaded.

expect.text: Choose a symbol and an as-of time, then Load, to see its tradable level map.

steps.title: Choosing a symbol to study
steps.narration: Typing AAPL into the Symbol field.
steps.point_out: The symbol field is ready for input.

steps.title: Choosing an as-of time
steps.narration: Typing in a specific date and time to study.
steps.point_out: The as-of field accepts a precise UTC timestamp.

steps.title: The price wall, unchanged
steps.narration: Clicking Load reveals the stock's strongest nearby price levels — exactly as this page has always shown them, undisturbed by this round's behind-the-scenes cleanup.
steps.point_out: The table's top resistance row spans roughly 300 to 302, marked Class A with a round-number flag, and the same band is drawn directly on the chart below.
